stem.en: You are on a beach. The ground shakes hard, and then the sea pulls far back from the shore. What should you do?

text.en: Walk out on the wet sand to see what is there

feedback.en: Never go to look. The sea pulling back can mean a tsunami is close.

text.en: Stay on the beach, as a low sea means no danger

feedback.en: A sea that pulls far back is a warning sign. The water is coming back.

text.en: Go to high ground at once, without waiting

feedback.en: Yes. Strong shaking and a sea pulling back are warning signs. There may be only minutes.

text.en: Wait on the beach until a phone alert arrives

feedback.en: Close to an earthquake, the water can arrive before any message does.

explanation.en: Strong shaking and a sea pulling far back are warning signs of a tsunami. Close to an earthquake the water can arrive in minutes, so go to high ground at once. Stay there until officials say it is safe, because a tsunami comes as a series of waves.

hints.en: Think of the people of Simeulue and how little time they had.
